claim: Alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma is a pediatric soft-tissue sarcoma caused by PAX3/7-FOXO1 fusion oncogenes.
source: Alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma is a pediatric soft-tissue sarcoma caused by PAX3/7-FOXO1 fusion oncogenes and is characterized by impaired skeletal muscle development.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field, supported by citations throughout the manuscript.

claim: Alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma is characterized by impaired skeletal muscle development.
source: Alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma is a pediatric soft-tissue sarcoma caused by PAX3/7-FOXO1 fusion oncogenes and is characterized by impaired skeletal muscle development.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the disease phenotype.

claim: PAX3-FOXO1 transgenic zebrafish develop tumors by 1.6–19 months.
source: Tumors developed by 1.6–19 months and were primitive neuroectodermal tumors or rhabdomyosarcoma.
evidence: This is a direct observation from the zebrafish model experiments.

claim: PAX3-FOXO1 transgenic zebrafish develop primitive neuroectodermal tumors or rhabdomyosarcoma.
source: Tumors developed by 1.6–19 months and were primitive neuroectodermal tumors or rhabdomyosarcoma.
evidence: This is based on histological analysis of tumors from the zebrafish model.

claim: her3 is a unique target of PAX3-FOXO1.
source: We applied this PAX3-FOXO1 transgenic zebrafish model to study how PAX3-FOXO1 leverages early developmental pathways for oncogenesis and found that her3 is a unique target.
evidence: This is based on microarray analysis and validation experiments in the zebrafish model.

claim: Ectopic expression of HES3 inhibits myogenesis in zebrafish.
source: Ectopic expression of the her3 human ortholog, HES3, inhibits myogenesis in zebrafish and mammalian cells, recapitulating the arrested muscle development characteristic of rhabdomyosarcoma.
evidence: This is demonstrated through experimental data showing reduced muscle marker expression in HES3-expressing zebrafish embryos.

claim: Ectopic expression of HES3 inhibits myogenesis in mammalian cells.
source: Ectopic expression of the her3 human ortholog, HES3, inhibits myogenesis in zebrafish and mammalian cells, recapitulating the arrested muscle development characteristic of rhabdomyosarcoma.
evidence: This is demonstrated through C2C12 differentiation assays showing reduced myogenic capacity.

claim: HES3 is overexpressed in fusion-positive versus fusion-negative tumors.
source: In patients, HES3 is overexpressed in fusion-positive versus fusion-negative tumors.
evidence: This is based on analysis of patient tumor RNA-seq and microarray data from multiple cohorts.

claim: HES3 overexpression is associated with reduced survival in patients in the context of the fusion.
source: Finally, HES3 overexpression is associated with reduced survival in patients in the context of the fusion.
evidence: This is based on survival analysis of patient data stratified by HES3 expression levels.

claim: Rhabdomyosarcoma presents as a solid tumor that displays characteristics of primitive skeletal muscle.
source: Rhabdomyosarcoma (RMS) presents as a solid tumor that displays characteristics of primitive skeletal muscle (Parham and Ellison, 2006).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: There are two major histological subtypes of rhabdomyosarcoma: embryonal (ERMS) and alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma (ARMS).
source: There are two major histological subtypes, embryonal (ERMS) and alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma (ARMS), with ARMS being more aggressive and particularly prone to metastasis (Williamson et al., 2010; Skapek et al., 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field supported by citations.

claim: ARMS is more aggressive and particularly prone to metastasis compared to ERMS.
source: There are two major histological subtypes, embryonal (ERMS) and alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma (ARMS), with ARMS being more aggressive and particularly prone to metastasis (Williamson et al., 2010; Skapek et al., 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: ERMS is characterized by frequent alterations affecting RAS signaling.
source: At the genomic level, ERMS is characterized by frequent alterations affecting RAS signaling, although this still represents a minority of the cases (Stratton et al., 1989; Langenau et al., 2007; Martinelli et al., 2009).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: The defining oncogenic event in ARMS is a t(1;13) or t(2;13) chromosomal translocation.
source: The defining oncogenic event in ARMS is a t(1;13) or t(2;13) chromosomal translocation in which the PAX7 or PAX3 DNA-binding domain, respectively, is fused to the FOXO1 transactivation domain to create a PAX3/7-FOXO1 chimeric oncogene (Barr et al., 1993; Galili et al., 1993; Shapiro et al., 1993; Davis et al., 1994).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: The PAX3-FOXO1 fusion is the most prevalent fusion in ARMS.
source: The PAX3-FOXO1 fusion is the most prevalent fusion in the disease, and functions as an aberrant transcription factor that is expressed in the nucleus and deregulates gene expression signatures (del Peso et al., 1999; Fredericks et al., 1995; Barber et al., 2002; Khan et al., 1999).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: PAX3-FOXO1 functions as an aberrant transcription factor that is expressed in the nucleus and deregulates gene expression signatures.
source: The PAX3-FOXO1 fusion is the most prevalent fusion in the disease, and functions as an aberrant transcription factor that is expressed in the nucleus and deregulates gene expression signatures (del Peso et al., 1999; Fredericks et al., 1995; Barber et al., 2002; Khan et al., 1999).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: PAX3/7-FOXO1 oncogenes remain intractable to therapeutic targeting.
source: The PAX3/7-FOXO1 oncogenes remain intractable to therapeutic targeting, impeding the development of effective precision medicine therapies.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of therapeutic development.

claim: Fusions are notoriously difficult to model in animals.
source: Fusions are notoriously difficult to model in animals, hence the limited availability of vertebrate animal models of this disease.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field.

claim: There is a narrow understanding of the cellular origin of RMS.
source: Furthermore, there is a narrow understanding of the cellular origin of RMS, making it difficult to define the expression pattern required for tumorigenesis (Hettmer and Wagers, 2010).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Beta-actin-driven PAX3-FOXO1 primarily produced primitive neuroectodermal tumors in a wild-type genetic background.
source: Beta-actin-driven PAX3-FOXO1 primarily produced primitive neuroectodermal tumors in a wild-type genetic background.
evidence: This is demonstrated by histological analysis shown in Figure 1B.

claim: CMV-driven PAX3-FOXO1 produced rhabdomyosarcoma in the tp53M214K/M214K-sensitized genetic background.
source: CMV-driven PAX3-FOXO1 produced rhabdomyosarcoma in the tp53M214K/M214K-sensitized genetic background.
evidence: This is demonstrated by histological analysis shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Ubiquitin-driven PAX3-FOXO1 produced an undifferentiated sarcoma in a wild-type genetic background.
source: Ubiquitin-driven PAX3-FOXO1 produced an undifferentiated sarcoma in a wild-type genetic background.
evidence: This is demonstrated by histological analysis shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Human PAX3-FOXO1 is expressed in fluorescent zebrafish tumors.
source: We performed RNA-seq on zebrafish tumors derived from all three promoters (beta actin, CMV, ubiquitin), and detected PAX3 and FOXO1 junction spanning reads indicating that human PAX3-FOXO1 is expressed in fluorescent tumors (Figure 1E, Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is demonstrated by RNA-seq data showing junction-spanning reads.

claim: The beta actin promoter driving PAX3-FOXO1 resulted in 9% tumor incidence in injected zebrafish.
source: Only a subset of the promoters that were tested induced tumor formation, including the beta actin (9% of injected zebrafish), CMV (16% of injected zebrafish), and ubiquitin (1.8% of injected zebrafish) promoters (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is based on counting tumors in injected zebrafish cohorts.

claim: The CMV promoter driving PAX3-FOXO1 resulted in 16% tumor incidence in injected zebrafish.
source: Only a subset of the promoters that were tested induced tumor formation, including the beta actin (9% of injected zebrafish), CMV (16% of injected zebrafish), and ubiquitin (1.8% of injected zebrafish) promoters (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is based on counting tumors in injected zebrafish cohorts.

claim: The ubiquitin promoter driving PAX3-FOXO1 resulted in 1.8% tumor incidence in injected zebrafish.
source: Only a subset of the promoters that were tested induced tumor formation, including the beta actin (9% of injected zebrafish), CMV (16% of injected zebrafish), and ubiquitin (1.8% of injected zebrafish) promoters (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is based on counting tumors in injected zebrafish cohorts.

claim: The fli1, unc503, mitfa, and gene trap approach driving PAX3-FOXO1 were not transforming.
source: The fli1, unc503, mitfa, and gene trap approach driving PAX3-FOXO1 were not transforming (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This is based on observation of no tumor formation in these cohorts.

claim: The beta actin promoter driving PAX3-FOXO1 is tumorigenic in zebrafish in both wildtype and p53-deficient genetic backgrounds.
source: The beta actin promoter driving the expression of PAX3-FOXO1 is tumorigenic in zebrafish, both in a wildtype and a p53-deficient genetic background.
evidence: This is based on tumor formation observed in both genetic backgrounds.

claim: BetaActin-PAX3FOXO1 tumors began developing at 3 months of age in 5% of injected zebrafish in the head.
source: In tp53 wild-type zebrafish, BetaActin-PAX3FOXO1 tumors began developing at 3 months of age in 5% of injected zebrafish in the head.
evidence: This is based on monitoring and histological analysis of zebrafish tumors.

claim: The majority of beta-actin-driven PAX3-FOXO1 zebrafish tumors were consistent with primitive neuroectodermal tumors.
source: Based on this analysis, the majority of beta-actin-driven PAX3-FOXO1 zebrafish tumors were consistent with primitive neuroectodermal tumors (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is based on histological analysis by a pathologist.

claim: The CMV promoter restricting PAX3-FOXO1 expression results in RMS tumors that present in the skeletal muscle of the back.
source: The CMV promoter restricting PAX3-FOXO1 expression results in RMS tumors that present in the skeletal muscle of the back.
evidence: This is based on observation and histological analysis of tumor location.

claim: CMV-driven PAX3-FOXO1 RMS tumors only develop in the context of the tp53M214K mutation.
source: This was true only in the context of the tp53M214K mutation, indicating that the tp53 mutation is sensitizing to and favors RMS.
evidence: This is based on observation that RMS only developed in tp53 mutant zebrafish.

claim: The tp53 mutation is sensitizing to and favors RMS development in zebrafish.
source: This was true only in the context of the tp53M214K mutation, indicating that the tp53 mutation is sensitizing to and favors RMS.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that RMS only develops in tp53 mutant background.

claim: The Pax3-Foxo1 RMS mouse model requires Tp53 deletion or other secondary cooperating mutations for RMS development.
source: These findings are concordant with the Pax3-Foxo1 RMS mouse model, in which Tp53 deletion, or other secondary cooperating mutations are required for RMS development (Keller et al., 2004).
evidence: This is established knowledge from the mouse model literature.

claim: Patients with Li Fraumeni syndrome develop RMS as part of the spectrum of the human disease.
source: Further, patients with Li Fraumeni syndrome develop RMS as part of the spectrum of the human disease (Li and Fraumeni, 1969).
evidence: This is established clinical knowledge supported by citation.

claim: PAX3-FOXO1 injected zebrafish exhibited reduced survival compared to PAX3 injected zebrafish during the first three days of life.
source: During the first three days of life, PAX3-FOXO1 injected zebrafish exhibited reduced survival as compared to PAX3 injected zebrafish (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is based on survival curve analysis shown in Figure 2C.

claim: PAX3-FOXO1 induced cyclopia in 30% of injected embryos.
source: Furthermore, PAX3-FOXO1-induced unique embryonic phenotypes, including cyclopia, which was present in 30% of injected embryos.
evidence: This is based on phenotypic scoring of injected embryos.

claim: Co-injection of PAX3-FOXO1 and a morpholino that knocks-down GFP-PAX3-FOXO1 expression eliminated the cyclopia phenotype.
source: Co-injection of PAX3-FOXO1 and a morpholino that knocks-down GFP-PAX3-FOXO1 expression eliminated the cyclopia phenotype (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is based on experimental data showing rescue of the phenotype with morpholino knockdown.

claim: PAX3-FOXO1 expression significantly reduced the number of GFP+ cells at 24 hr post-fertilization compared to PAX3.
source: Fluorescent activated cell sorting (FACS) showed that PAX3-FOXO1 expression significantly reduced the number of GFP + cells at 24 hr post-fertilization as compared to PAX3 (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is based on FACS quantification data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Only 3% of adult zebrafish had detectable GFP-PAX3FOXO1 expression with resulting tumor development or asymmetric skeletal muscle.
source: We found that only 3% of adult zebrafish had detectable GFP-PAX3FOXO1 expression with resulting tumor development or asymmetric skeletal muscle (Figure 2F–G).
evidence: This is based on screening adult zebrafish for fluorescence and phenotypes.

claim: PAX3-FOXO1-injected embryos had an increase in the number of TUNEL-positive cells undergoing apoptosis compared to GFP controls and PAX3 in wild-type zebrafish.
source: PAX3-FOXO1-injected embryos had an increase in the number of TUNEL-positive cells undergoing apoptosis as compared to GFP controls and PAX3 in wild-type zebrafish (Figure 2I).
evidence: This is based on TUNEL staining quantification shown in Figure 2I.

claim: tp53M214K mutant zebrafish embryos are unable to invoke an appropriate response to PAX3-FOXO1+ cells, resulting in a gross reduction in survival by 3 days of age.
source: We found that tp53M214K mutant zebrafish embryos are unable to invoke an appropriate response to PAX3-FOXO1 + cells, resulting in a gross reduction in survival by 3 days of age (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is based on survival analysis comparing wildtype and tp53 mutant embryos.

claim: CMV-PAX3FOXO1+ cells are more abundant in tp53M214K injected mutant zebrafish compared to their wild-type counterparts by 28 hr post fertilization.
source: Further, injected CMV-PAX3FOXO1 + cells are more abundant in tp53M214K injected mutant zebrafish as compared to their wild-type counterparts by 28 hr post fertilization (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C–D).
evidence: This is based on quantification of GFP-positive pixels in embryos.

claim: The increase in GFP-PAX3FOXO1+ cells in tp53M214K mutant zebrafish is coupled with a reduction in the ratio of TUNEL-positive cells.
source: This significant increase in the number of GFP-PAX3FOXO1 + cells is coupled with a reduction in the ratio of TUNEL-positive cells, indicating that tp53M214K mutant zebrafish provide a susceptible environment for PAX3-FOXO1 + cellular persistence and ultimately tumor development (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E–G; Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is based on TUNEL staining quantification in tp53 mutant embryos.

claim: PAX3 and PAX3-FOXO1 act as transcription factors in zebrafish.
source: After comparing differentially expressed genes versus the GFP injected control for PAX3 and PAX3-FOXO1, the most highly enriched Gene Ontology (GO) terms indicated that PAX3 and PAX3-FOXO1 act as transcription factors (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is based on Gene Ontology analysis of microarray data.

claim: PAX3-positive cells were most indicative of the neural plate, neuroectoderm, or ectoderm.
source: PAX3-positive cells were most indicative of the neural plate, neuroectoderm, or ectoderm, whereas PAX3-FOXO1 was indicative of a somite, segmental plate, or optic vesicle and immature eye (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is based on DAVID analysis of enriched genes from microarray data.

claim: PAX3-FOXO1 was indicative of a somite, segmental plate, or optic vesicle and immature eye.
source: PAX3-positive cells were most indicative of the neural plate, neuroectoderm, or ectoderm, whereas PAX3-FOXO1 was indicative of a somite, segmental plate, or optic vesicle and immature eye (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is based on DAVID analysis of enriched genes from microarray data.

claim: PAX3 and PAX3-FOXO1 expression changes are distinct and show statistical significance in a developmental context.
source: We then performed a principal component analysis (PCA) and found that PAX3 and PAX3-FOXO1 expression changes are distinct and show statistical significance in a developmental context (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is based on PCA analysis of microarray data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: PAX3 and PAX3-FOXO1 up-regulated 118 shared genes.
source: We found that PAX3 and PAX3-FOXO1 up-regulated 118 shared genes, whereas PAX3-FOXO1 uniquely induced 529 genes.
evidence: This is based on analysis of microarray data comparing gene expression.

claim: PAX3-FOXO1 uniquely induced 529 genes.
source: We found that PAX3 and PAX3-FOXO1 up-regulated 118 shared genes, whereas PAX3-FOXO1 uniquely induced 529 genes.
evidence: This is based on analysis of microarray data comparing gene expression.

claim: her3 was the most highly induced gene unique to PAX3-FOXO1 expression with a 21-fold increase compared to the GFP control.
source: The most highly induced gene unique to PAX3-FOXO1 expression was her3, with a 21-fold increase as compared to the GFP control (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is based on microarray data analysis shown in Figure 3D.

claim: her3 induction was unique to PAX3-FOXO1 and not induced by PAX3.
source: This analysis indicated that her3 induction was unique to PAX3-FOXO1 (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is based on qRT-PCR validation of microarray results.

claim: her3 expression is dependent on the PAX3-FOXO1 oncogene.
source: These data suggest that her3 is a novel target of PAX3-FOXO1 in vivo, that her3 is not induced by PAX3, and that her3 expression is dependent on the PAX3-FOXO1 oncogene.
evidence: This is based on morpholino knockdown experiments showing reduced her3 expression when PAX3-FOXO1 is knocked down.

claim: Rhabdomyosarcoma tumors express early markers along the skeletal muscle lineage such as MYOD1, MYOG and Desmin but fail to terminally differentiate.
source: A hallmark of rhabdomyosarcoma is that tumors express early markers along the skeletal muscle lineage such as MYOD1, MYOG and Desmin; however, these tumors fail to terminally differentiate indicating a developmental arrest (Parham and Ellison, 2006; Saab et al., 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge about RMS pathology supported by citations.

claim: PAX3-FOXO1 did not affect the mRNA levels of myod or myog by 24hpf.
source: We found that PAX3-FOXO1 did not affect the mRNA levels of myod or myog; however, by 24hpf there was a significant reduction in the expression of myl1 and myhz2.
evidence: This is based on qRT-PCR analysis of muscle markers in injected zebrafish embryos.

claim: PAX3-FOXO1 caused a significant reduction in the expression of myl1 and myhz2 by 24hpf.
source: We found that PAX3-FOXO1 did not affect the mRNA levels of myod or myog; however, by 24hpf there was a significant reduction in the expression of myl1 and myhz2.
evidence: This is based on qRT-PCR analysis of muscle markers in injected zebrafish embryos.

claim: Overexpression of HES3 alone inhibited terminal muscle differentiation.
source: Surprisingly, overexpression of HES3 alone had a similar effect of inhibiting terminal muscle differentiation, indicating that her3/HES3 contribute to maintaining a more primitive cellular state.
evidence: This is based on qRT-PCR analysis showing reduced expression of terminal differentiation markers.

claim: PAX3-FOXO1 and HES3 together had no significant additive effect on muscle differentiation.
source: Together, PAX3-FOXO1 and HES3 had no significant additive effect, suggesting they are functioning in a linear pathway with her3/HES3 being downstream of PAX3-FOXO1 (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is based on qRT-PCR analysis of muscle markers with co-injection experiments.

claim: Co-injection of HES3 allowed PAX3-FOXO1 cells to survive and/or proliferate, with a greater number of GFP-positive pixels persisting by 72hpf.
source: Co-injection of HES3 allowed PAX3-FOXO1 cells to survive and/or proliferate, with a greater number of GFP-positive pixels and thus PAX3-FOXO1 positive cells persisting by 72hpf (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is based on quantification of GFP-positive pixels at different timepoints.

claim: HES3 promotes a more tolerant cellular environment allowing for survival with expression of the highly toxic PAX3-FOXO1.
source: These results suggest that HES3 promotes a more tolerant cellular environment allowing for survival with expression of the highly toxic PAX3-FOXO1.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that HES3 co-expression increases PAX3-FOXO1+ cell persistence.

claim: HES3 overexpression in zebrafish allows for PAX3-FOXO1+ cells to either inappropriately persist or divide, resulting in an increased number of observable GFP-PAX3FOXO1+ pixels by 24 hr post-fertilization.
source: By implementing our CMV injected mosaic zebrafish models, we found that HES3 overexpression in zebrafish allows for PAX3-FOXO1+ cells to either inappropriately persist or divide, resulting in an increased number of observable GFP-PAX3FOXO1 + pixels by 24 hr post-fertilization (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: This is based on quantification of GFP-positive pixels in co-injected embryos.

claim: HES3 alone does not induce apoptosis in zebrafish embryos.
source: We performed TUNEL assays on these same zebrafish embryos and found that HES3 alone does not induce apoptosis.
evidence: This is based on TUNEL staining analysis of HES3-injected embryos.

claim: There is no significant difference in the normalized ratio of TUNEL cells for PAX3-FOXO1-injected embryos compared to PAX3-FOXO1 + HES3.
source: Further, there is no significant difference in the normalized ratio of TUNEL cells for PAX3-FOXO1-injected embryos as compared to PAX3-FOXO1 + HES3 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D–E).
evidence: This is based on TUNEL staining quantification in co-injected embryos.

claim: PAX3-FOXO1 + HES3 cooperation facilitates PAX3-FOXO1+ cells to persist during embryogenesis independently of apoptosis inhibition at 24hpf.
source: These data indicate that PAX3-FOXO1 + HES3 cooperation facilitates PAX3-FOXO1 + cells to persist during embryogenesis independently of apoptosis inhibition at this timepoint (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that HES3 increases PAX3-FOXO1+ cell numbers without reducing apoptosis.

claim: By day 6 of differentiation, MyoD, MyoG, Myl1, and Myh1 exhibited significant inhibition of expression in C2C12-HES3 overexpressing cells compared to C2C12-Empty controls.
source: By day 6 of differentiation, MyoD, MyoG, Myl1, and Myh1 exhibited significant inhibition of expression in C2C12-HES3 overexpressing cells as compared to the C2C12-Empty controls.
evidence: This is based on qRT-PCR analysis of muscle markers in differentiated C2C12 cells.

claim: Myl1 and Myh1 were the most affected by HES3 overexpression at fusion day 6, with a 2.9–3.2 fold decrease in expression levels.
source: Moreover, Myl1 and Myh1, which represent terminal muscle differentiation, were the most affected by HES3 overexpression at fusion day 6, with a 2.9–3.2 fold decrease in expression levels, as compared to a 1.8–1.9 fold decrease observed for MyoD and MyoG (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is based on qRT-PCR quantification of gene expression in C2C12 cells.

claim: There was 2.3X more myogenic nuclei in C2C12-Empty compared to C2C12-HES3 overexpressing cells.
source: After analyzing the percentage of myogenic nuclei, or the nuclei within a myofiber, there was 2.3X more myogenic nuclei in C2C12-Empty as compared to the C2C12-HES3 overexpressing cells (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is based on immunofluorescence quantification of myogenic nuclei.

claim: The fusion index indicated a significant reduction in the fusion capacity of HES3 overexpressing cells.
source: Furthermore, the fusion index (myogenic nuclei with > 3 nuclei present per myofiber) indicated a significant reduction in the fusion capacity of HES3 overexpressing cells (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is based on quantification of multi-nucleated myotubes.

claim: HES3 overexpression modified the kinetics of C2C12 differentiation, with myosin protein being undetectable at day 4 of fusion in C2C12-HES3 overexpressing cells and detectable in C2C12 controls.
source: HES3 overexpression also modified the kinetics of C2C12 differentiation, with myosin protein being undetectable at day 4 of fusion in C2C12-HES3 overexpressing cells and detectable in C2C12 controls (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: This is based on Western blot analysis of myosin protein expression.

claim: HES3 is inhibiting the differentiation process and promoting a more primitive cellular state in mammalian systems.
source: Hence, HES3 is inhibiting the differentiation process and promoting a more primitive cellular state in mammalian systems.
evidence: This is inferred from multiple lines of evidence showing reduced differentiation markers and fusion capacity.

claim: HES3 accelerated the cellular accumulation of Rh30 cells.
source: To determine if HES3 modified the proliferation kinetics of Rh30, cells were plated at a low density and timepoints evaluated from days 1 to 6. We found that in this context HES3 accelerated the cellular accumulation of Rh30 (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is based on crystal violet staining assay measuring cell accumulation.

claim: HES3 overexpression in Rh30 cells caused >300 fold down-regulation of Missing in Metastasis (MTSS1).
source: Notably, there was > 300 fold down-regulation of Missing in Metastasis (MTSS1), and an up-regulation of matrix metallopeptidases 3 and 9 (MMP3 and MMP9) (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is based on qPCR array analysis of metastasis-associated genes.

claim: HES3 overexpression in Rh30 cells caused up-regulation of matrix metallopeptidases 3 and 9 (MMP3 and MMP9).
source: Notably, there was > 300 fold down-regulation of Missing in Metastasis (MTSS1), and an up-regulation of matrix metallopeptidases 3 and 9 (MMP3 and MMP9) (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is based on qPCR array analysis of metastasis-associated genes.

claim: HES3 significantly accelerated the growth kinetics of C2C12 cells when plated at sub-confluent levels over the course of 6 days.
source: HES3 was then evaluated for its ability to modulate cellular accumulation. HES3 significantly accelerated the growth kinetics of C2C12 cells when plated at sub-confluent levels over the course of 6 days (Figure 6F).
evidence: This is based on crystal violet staining assay measuring cell accumulation.

claim: HES3 overexpression significantly increased the number of colonies that formed in soft agar.
source: These same cells were plated in suspension in soft agar and cultured for one month to determine the colony formation capacity. HES3 overexpression significantly increased the number of colonies that formed (Figure 6G).
evidence: This is based on soft agar colony formation assay.

claim: HES3 alters the expression of genes that are PAX3-FOXO1 direct targets or whose expression is modified by PAX3-FOXO1, including MyoG, Igf2, and Hoxc6.
source: This is complemented by data indicating that HES3 alters the expression of genes that are PAX3-FOXO1 direct targets or whose expression is modified by PAX3-FOXO1; including, MyoG, Igf2, and Hoxc6 (Figure 6H) (Khan et al., 1999; Lagha et al., 2010).
evidence: This is based on qPCR array analysis of rhabdomyosarcoma-associated genes.

claim: HES3 had higher expression levels in fusion-positive RMS compared to fusion-negative RMS in three independent tumor cohorts.
source: We analyzed RNA-Seq and HuEx array data from three independent RMS tumor cohorts, together representing the largest collection of over 200 sequenced RMS tumors (Chen et al., 2013; Shern et al., 2014). We found that HES3 had higher expression levels in fusion-positive RMS as compared to fusion-negative RMS (Figure 7A–C).
evidence: This is based on analysis of patient tumor RNA-seq and microarray data from multiple cohorts.

claim: The overexpression of HES3 is associated with reduced overall survival in PAX3/7-FOXO1 fusion-positive RMS patients.
source: Significantly, in RMS patients, the overexpression of HES3 is associated with reduced overall survival in PAX3/7-FOXO1 fusion-positive RMS patients, but not in fusion-negative RMS patients (Figure 7D).
evidence: This is based on survival analysis of patient data stratified by HES3 expression and fusion status.

claim: HES3 overexpression is not associated with reduced survival in fusion-negative RMS patients.
source: Significantly, in RMS patients, the overexpression of HES3 is associated with reduced overall survival in PAX3/7-FOXO1 fusion-positive RMS patients, but not in fusion-negative RMS patients (Figure 7D).
evidence: This is based on survival analysis showing no significant association in fusion-negative patients.

claim: FGFR4, ALK, and PARP1 are concordantly overexpressed with HES3 in RMS tumors.
source: A subset of clinically relevant kinases and molecular targets was identified as being concordantly overexpressed with HES3; namely, FGFR4, ALK, and PARP1 (Figure 7E).
evidence: This is based on differential gene expression analysis between HES3 high and low tumors.

claim: HES3 is a member of the HES family of basic helix-loop-helix transcription factors.
source: HES3 is a member of the HES family of basic helix-loop-helix transcription factors, which function as direct or indirect transcriptional activators or repressors, thus regulating gene expression and epigenetic identity (Kageyama et al., 2007).
evidence: This is established knowledge about HES3 supported by citation.

claim: HES3 is expressed in the developing brain and inhibits differentiation of neural stem cells.
source: HES3 is expressed in the developing brain and inhibits differentiation of neural stem cells (Hatakeyama et al., 2004).
evidence: This is established knowledge about HES3 function supported by citation.

claim: HES3 is expressed in glioblastoma cell culture and co-localizes with additional markers of stemness in the mouse brain.
source: In cancer, HES3 is expressed in glioblastoma cell culture, and co-localizes with additional markers of stemness in the mouse brain (Park et al., 2013; Poser et al., 2013; Katoh and Katoh, 2007).
evidence: This is established knowledge about HES3 in cancer supported by citations.

claim: HES3's role as a cooperating gene in PAX3/7-FOXO1 fusion-positive rhabdomyosarcoma has never been described before this study.
source: However, its role as a cooperating gene in PAX3/7-FOXO1 fusion-positive rhabdomyosarcoma has never been described.
evidence: This is a statement about the novelty of the findings in this manuscript.

claim: PAX3-FOXO1 exhibits discrete cell lineage susceptibility and transformation.
source: We developed human PAX3-FOXO1 -driven zebrafish models of tumorigenesis and found that PAX3-FOXO1 exhibits discrete cell lineage susceptibility and transformation.
evidence: This is based on observation that different promoters driving PAX3-FOXO1 produce different tumor types.

claim: Human PAX3-FOXO1 under the control of different promoters had unique survival and transforming properties suggesting cell-of-origin specificity to oncogenesis.
source: Human PAX3-FOXO1 under the control of different promoters had unique survival and transforming properties suggesting cell-of-origin specificity to oncogenesis.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that different promoters produce different outcomes.

claim: Tested promoters had a negative impact on early survival (up to 30 days of life), but to different extents.
source: Tested promoters had a negative impact on early survival (up to 30 days of life), but to different extents (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on survival curve analysis of different promoter-driven PAX3-FOXO1 zebrafish.

claim: The human fusion-oncogene is transforming in zebrafish when expressed in a variety of cellular contexts.
source: These data demonstrate that the human fusion-oncogene is transforming in zebrafish when expressed in a variety of cellular contexts and that some, but not all, cellular identities are susceptible to transformation.
evidence: This is based on observation that multiple promoters can drive tumor formation.

claim: Some, but not all, cellular identities are susceptible to PAX3-FOXO1 transformation.
source: These data demonstrate that the human fusion-oncogene is transforming in zebrafish when expressed in a variety of cellular contexts and that some, but not all, cellular identities are susceptible to transformation.
evidence: This is based on observation that some promoters do not produce tumors.

claim: Rhabdomyosarcoma only develops in the tp53M214K background, predominantly with the CMV promoter as compared to the beta actin promoter.
source: Rhabdomyosarcoma only develops in the tp53M214K background, predominantly with the CMV promoter as compared to the beta actin promoter.
evidence: This is based on histological analysis of tumors from different genetic backgrounds and promoters.

claim: PAX3-FOXO1 regulation of HES3 is likely indirect.
source: PAX3-FOXO1 regulation of HES3 is likely indirect. Chip-seq data from rhabdomyosarcoma cell culture indicates that PAX3-FOXO1 does not bind the HES3 promoter; however, these results may differ in a dynamic developmental context (Cao et al., 2010).
evidence: This is based on ChIP-seq data from the literature showing no direct binding.

claim: Copy number analysis of fusion-positive patient RMS tumors finds no amplification of HES3.
source: Copy number analysis of fusion-positive patient RMS tumors finds no amplification of HES3, indicating up-regulation is at the transcriptional level.
evidence: This is based on analysis of patient tumor genomic data.

claim: PAX3-FOXO1 and HES3 function linearly, with HES3 being downstream of PAX3-FOXO1.
source: Our data suggest that PAX3-FOXO1 and HES3 function linearly, with HES3 being downstream of PAX3-FOXO1.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that they have similar effects without additive effects.

claim: HES3 contributes to more aggressive disease in patients when overexpressed in the context of the PAX3-FOXO1 fusion.
source: HES3 contributes to more aggressive disease in patients when overexpressed in the context of the PAX3-FOXO1 fusion, likely by a multi-variate platform of: (1) inhibiting terminal muscle differentiation, (2) modifying cellular plasticity to make cells that acquire the PAX3-FOXO1 fusion more tolerant of its expression, and (3) inducing additional transcriptional changes.
evidence: This is inferred from multiple lines of evidence including survival analysis and functional studies.

claim: PAX3-FOXO1 induction of HES3 expression in a mesodermal lineage is ectopic.
source: PAX3-FOXO1 induction of HES3 expression in a mesodermal lineage is ectopic, and HES3 plays no known role in normal somitogenesis or myogenesis.
evidence: This is based on knowledge that HES3 is normally expressed in neural tissues, not muscle.

claim: HES3 plays no known role in normal somitogenesis or myogenesis.
source: PAX3-FOXO1 induction of HES3 expression in a mesodermal lineage is ectopic, and HES3 plays no known role in normal somitogenesis or myogenesis.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about HES3 function in development.

claim: HES3 allows for PAX3-FOXO1 cells to inappropriately persist during embryogenesis independently of inhibiting apoptosis.
source: We note that HES3 allows for PAX3-FOXO1 cells to inappropriately persist during embryogenesis independently of inhibiting apoptosis.
evidence: This is based on experimental data showing increased PAX3-FOXO1+ cells without reduced apoptosis.

claim: In human fusion-positive RMS, which typically lack TP53 mutations, HES3 overexpression could represent an alternative mechanism to facilitate PAX3-FOXO1+ cell persistence and tumor initiation events.
source: In human fusion-positive RMS, which typically lack TP53 mutations (Shern et al., 2014), HES3 overexpression could represent an alternative mechanism to facilitate PAX3-FOXO1 + cell persistence and tumor initiation events.
evidence: This is speculation based on the observation that HES3 promotes cell persistence in zebrafish.

claim: MTSS1 is a target of the PAX3-FOXO1 fusion.
source: Previous studies indicate that MTSS1 is a target of the PAX3-FOXO1 fusion (Ebauer et al., 2007); therefore, the modification of MTSS1 expression, and additional genes integral in cell invasion could occur in part through PAX3-FOXO1 induction of HES3.
evidence: This is established knowledge from previous studies supported by citation.

claim: The modification of MTSS1 expression and additional genes integral in cell invasion could occur in part through PAX3-FOXO1 induction of HES3.
source: Previous studies indicate that MTSS1 is a target of the PAX3-FOXO1 fusion (Ebauer et al., 2007); therefore, the modification of MTSS1 expression, and additional genes integral in cell invasion could occur in part through PAX3-FOXO1 induction of HES3.
evidence: This is speculation based on the observation that HES3 modifies MTSS1 expression.

claim: Stratifying patient tumor data between HES3 high and low expressing RMS elucidated translational molecular targets with immediate potential applications in the clinic such as co-expression of FGFR4, ALK, and PARP1.
source: Most significantly, stratifying patient tumor data between HES3 high and low expressing RMS elucidated translational molecular targets with immediate potential applications in the clinic such as co-expression of FGFR4, ALK, and PARP1.
evidence: This is based on differential gene expression analysis of patient tumors stratified by HES3 expression.

claim: Zebrafish are a complementary model system that can address genetic and cellular issues in cancer research.
source: Zebrafish are a complementary model system that can address these genetic and cellular issues.
evidence: This is a general statement about the utility of zebrafish models.

claim: Zebrafish systems provide insight into the underlying biology of how cancer genes behave in a complex environment.
source: Advantages of zebrafish systems are two-fold: (1) they provide insight into the underlying biology of how cancer genes behave in a complex environment and (2) provide a platform for translational drug discovery efforts.
evidence: This is a general statement about the advantages of zebrafish models.

claim: Zebrafish systems provide a platform for translational drug discovery efforts.
source: Advantages of zebrafish systems are two-fold: (1) they provide insight into the underlying biology of how cancer genes behave in a complex environment and (2) provide a platform for translational drug discovery efforts.
evidence: This is a general statement about the advantages of zebrafish models.

claim: The tumor presentation spectrum identified three distinct cellular contexts that are susceptible to transformation.
source: The tumor presentation spectrum identified three distinct cellular contexts that are susceptible to transformation, generating insight into basic mechanisms of PAX3-FOXO1 tumorigenesis and human rhabdomyosarcoma.
evidence: This is based on observation of three different tumor types from different promoters.

claim: her3 is a transcription factor that contains a DNA-binding domain, an orange domain, and a tetrapeptide motif at the C terminus.
source: her3 is a transcription factor that contains a DNA-binding domain, an orange domain, and a tetrapeptide motif at the C terminus (Hans et al., 2004).
evidence: This is established knowledge about her3 structure supported by citation.

claim: In zebrafish and mouse models, her3 is expressed in the neuroepithelial stem cells of the neural plate and inhibits their premature differentiation.
source: In zebrafish and mouse models, her3 is expressed in the neuroepithelial stem cells of the neural plate and inhibits their premature differentiation (Hatakeyama et al., 2004).
evidence: This is established knowledge about her3 function supported by citation.

claim: HES3 acts as both a transcriptional repressor and activator, by indirectly or directly influencing transcription depending on its sub-cellular localization.
source: HES3 acts as both a transcriptional repressor and activator, by indirectly or directly influencing transcription depending on its sub-cellular localization.
evidence: This is established knowledge about HES3 function.

claim: ChIP-seq data from rhabdomyosarcoma cell culture indicates that PAX3-FOXO1 does not bind the HES3 promoter.
source: Chip-seq data from rhabdomyosarcoma cell culture indicates that PAX3-FOXO1 does not bind the HES3 promoter; however, these results may differ in a dynamic developmental context (Cao et al., 2010).
evidence: This is based on published ChIP-seq data from the literature.

claim: HES3 is acting as a transcriptional activator and repressor, consistent with its role in normal development.
source: Potentially, HES3 is acting as a transcriptional activator and repressor, consistent with its role in normal development.
evidence: This is speculation based on observed gene expression changes and known HES3 function.

claim: This zebrafish RMS model represents a novel strategy to identify new targets and biomarkers in the context of human disease.
source: Taken together, this model represents a novel strategy to identify new targets and biomarkers in the context of human disease and contributes to our understanding of RMS biology by defining the earliest tumor initiation events.
evidence: This is a summary statement about the significance of the model.

claim: This zebrafish RMS model contributes to our understanding of RMS biology by defining the earliest tumor initiation events.
source: Taken together, this model represents a novel strategy to identify new targets and biomarkers in the context of human disease and contributes to our understanding of RMS biology by defining the earliest tumor initiation events.
evidence: This is a summary statement about the significance of the model.
